meta.how_to_use: Run one stage per session in build_order. Before a stage, read its context_to_read and nothing else. A stage with needs_backend starts only when those requests are done in the backend plan, or it builds the named fallback. Each stage ends with its stage checks (conventions.stage_checks) and a report in progress_log. End-to-end, accessibility, performance and security tests of both deliverables run together in FT1a and FT1b.

findings.handling: Both surfaces use the hosted sign-in and sign-up as the backend serves them (password plus code; one-time code sign-in for daily login). No own sign-up form is designed here (PW1, PP1).

findings.handling: The compact onboarding (PW2) replaces it for the pilot. Assisted onboarding is NX-07.

findings.finding: An existing car owner who chooses 'Create a business' was sent to the full portal. In the consumer PWA the business choice of W-ONB-01 still points to a placeholder URL.
findings.handling: PW2: 'Service provider' in W-ONB-01 and 'Create a business' in the account menu open the compact onboarding. Vendor and fleet choices keep the portal link.

findings.finding: Step 7 (call-back code, licence upload, review in 2 days, Verified badge) is larger than what the owner now wants in the MVP.
findings.handling: Optional licence upload and 'Verification pending' only (PW2, PP4). The rest is NX-02.

findings.handling: PP5 (dashboard) and a short 'Finish your profile' card on Today (PW1) that lists what the compact onboarding skipped.

global_decisions.decision: Two deliverables in two apps. D1, the provider Web UI, is the route group /<locale>/provider of the business web app at web.<DOMAIN> (frontend/, client cp-web-portal, portal BFF). D2, the Workshop PWA, is the route group /<locale>/provider of the consumer PWA at pwa.<DOMAIN> (pwa/, client cp-web-consumer, consumer BFF). The Workshop PWA has its own web app manifest (id and scope /<locale>/provider/, start_url /<locale>/provider/today) so it can be added to the home screen as its own app.
global_decisions.why: Owner decision PRV-OQ-01. The consumer PWA already has the BFF, hosted sign-in, upload kit, map, service worker and push, and Reza gets one sign-in for his family car and his shop (Docs/11 Ch.3).
consequences: The consumer BFF forwards a fixed list of provider operations (PRV-BR-08). Docs/40 SEC-WEB-5 and the header comment of pwa/src/server/bff/allowlist.ts change.
Business pushes arrive in the consumer PWA's service worker. Docs/90 line 124 and pwa DI-16 change (PRV-DI-06, PRV-BR-09).
'Open in Web UI' crosses origins: new tab, separate sign-in.
The camera is allowed on the consumer origin (SEC-WEB-4), so no workaround is needed.
global_decisions.checked: pwa/src/server/bff/allowlist.ts refuses every /v1/orgs/{org_id} route except fleet driver routes today. backend/libs/auth has no rule that binds organization operations to a client; tokens carry no roles (SEC-AU-3). The backend confirms this in PRV-BR-08.

global_decisions.decision: The Workshop PWA does: (1) compact onboarding, (2) answer appointment requests, (3) update and close jobs, (4) reply to customers (review replies, approval answers, comments on the shop's content), (5) post before/after photos. Plus sign-in, business switch, Today, notifications and push, language, theme. Every other task is a link 'Open in Web UI' and is not re-implemented.
global_decisions.why: Owner scope of 2026-11-15 plus PRV-OQ-02 and PRV-OQ-03.

global_decisions.decision: The server decides access. Both deliverables show actions from Appointment.allowed_transitions, the caller's role (P* or P+ as each operation's sec line says) and plan entitlements. No rule is copied to the client. A 403 for a staff member shows 'Ask the owner'.
global_decisions.why: Same rule as the fleet option in frontend/README.md.

global_decisions.decision: Phone budgets for the Workshop PWA: the /provider routes add at most 120 KB gzip of route JavaScript on top of the PWA's shared chunks, LCP ≤ 2.5 s on a mid-range phone over throttled 4G, 48 px targets, one primary action per screen, Sunlight theme offered on first run. The map loads only on the location step of the compact onboarding. Photos are resized in the browser to ≤ 2048 px on the long side (about ≤ 600 KB) before media.upload_init.
global_decisions.why: Docs/carpal-design-system: workshop yards, sun, greasy hands, mobile data. Measured in FT1b.

global_decisions.decision: Provider API answers are never cached by the service worker or kept in Web Storage (they carry customer data); the worker's shell cache is wiped at sign-out, as pwa P12 does. Photos are taken through the upload kit's file input with capture.

AI output is always a labelled draft. A person edits and publishes; the client never sends or publishes AI text without a tap. With AI off (flag, plan or consent) the same screens work with empty editors.

Roles are those of Docs/40 §0.5: provider_owner, provider_manager (P+), provider_staff (P*). The team page offers these three. A technician's 'assigned jobs only' is a 'My jobs' filter built from appointment participants.

Components used by both apps live in a new package shared/business-ui (linked like @carpal/i18n): request card, pre-visit report, answer sheets, job status and close form, review card, reply editor with AI draft, approval card, comment thread, showcase composer steps, status chips. They take data and callbacks as props and import no BFF client, router or app shell. Each app wraps them in its own pages. The package is created in PW1 and grows in PW3-PW7; the Web UI stages reuse it.
global_decisions.why: The two deliverables are two apps (PRV-GD-01); this is the default of PU-OQ-01.

global_decisions.decision: Backend work is not done in this plan. Requests are listed in backend_requests with a fallback and handed to backend/BR-update-plan.json (intake_candidates_provider_plan). A frontend stage names the requests it needs and either waits or builds the fallback.

Stage checks only until the end: typecheck, lint, unit and component tests, and a manual smoke of the stage's path against the dev backend. Playwright journeys, axe, performance and security tests of both deliverables run together in FT1a and FT1b.
global_decisions.why: Owner: the plan (PWA and Web UI) is tested together at the final stage.

global_decisions.decision: The layout follows the mockup. Parts-related areas that the pilot does not deliver stay where the mockup has them, greyed out and disabled, with the label 'Coming soon': the Web UI navigation entries Parts and Job log, and any 'Find a part', 'Ask about this part' or 'Request trade access' action on a request or job page. A disabled entry has aria-disabled, is skipped by the keyboard, opens no page and calls no operation. Typing the parts used when closing a job is not part of this: it stays enabled.
global_decisions.why: Owner, 2026-11-16: do not remove, only disable. The pilot shows where the parts flow will be without PX1.

conventions.stage_size: One stage = one session. Load is rated small, medium or full. A full stage has a split_point: if the session runs long, stop there, report, and continue as '<id>b' in the next session.
conventions.context_rule: Read only the stage's context_to_read. Use the generated operation map of shared/api-contracts instead of re-reading Docs/40 blocks. Copy the pattern of the first finished screen of a kind.
conventions.stage_checks: pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm test in every package the stage touched (pwa/, frontend business app, shared/business-ui); manual smoke in FA and EN at 360 px for PW stages and at 1280 px for PP stages. Use Node 24.
conventions.report: Add to progress_log: date, stage, what was built, deviations, backend requests met or replaced by a fallback, notes for the next stage.

screens.name: Start a business
screens.content: Entry from W-ONB-01 'Service provider' and from the account menu. Business name, type, phone, terms, AI analysis consent (provider_analytics_ai_use, optional).

screens.name: Where is the workshop
screens.content: 'Use my location' or a pin on the map, typed address, pin check warning, show exact address or area only.

screens.name: What you repair
screens.content: Service systems as chips (at least one), brands as chips with search (at least one). Models, series and tasks are added later in the Web UI.

screens.name: Hours and go live
screens.content: Working days and hours with one preset, optional licence photo, summary, Publish. Result: live with 'Verification pending' and a list of what to finish later.

screens.name: Today
screens.content: Counters: new requests (oldest age, average response time), replies waiting, photos waiting for the customer. Today's jobs. Safety-critical requests first. 'Finish your profile' card.

screens.name: Requests
screens.content: Segments New · Proposed · Upcoming; cards with vehicle, problem, urgency, preferred time, age, safety mark; 'My jobs' filter.

screens.name: Request detail
screens.content: Customer display name and 'first visit'; vehicle and mileage; AI pre-visit summary or 'Triage: not provided'; photos and video; shared history or 'Not shared by customer'; preferred times; AI slot suggestion with the day's load; coverage mismatch note; customer-visible messages; actions Accept · Propose time · More.

screens.name: Answer sheets
screens.content: Accept (time, duration), Propose time (chips for 14 days, note), Decline (reason chips, note), Ask for information (message to the customer; status stays provider_reviewing).

screens.name: Update job / Close job
screens.content: Status buttons from allowed_transitions: In progress, Awaiting parts (note, estimated completion, cost range), Ready for pickup. Close job: service system and task prefilled, labour cost, parts cost, optional part lines (name, part number, quantity), warranty note, invoice photo, internal note.

screens.name: Replies
screens.content: Tabs Reviews · Comments · Approvals with counts.

screens.name: Reply to a review
screens.content: Review and context; labelled AI draft with tone chips in an editable box; AI risk note; Publish reply; Save draft; 'Flag or request mediation' opens the Web UI.

screens.name: Approval request
screens.content: 'Do you recognise this customer?' with display name, date and kind of work only; the answers the contract allows; note for CarPal; days left; 'A low rating is never a reason to say no'.

screens.name: Reply to a comment
screens.content: Showcase or post card, the thread, a reply box that posts as the shop, Report comment.

screens.name: Photos
screens.content: Showcases with status (Draft, Waiting for customer, Being reviewed, Live, Declined); 'Jobs ready for photos'.

screens.name: New before/after
screens.content: Pick a completed appointment; Before and After photos from camera or gallery, up to 10, progress per photo.

screens.name: Check and caption
screens.content: AI pairs, plate and face flags with Blur (default) or Keep, caption draft and tags as editable chips, cover photo.

screens.name: Send for customer approval
screens.content: Preview; ask the customer to approve; optional share to the feed; result with the next step.

screens.name: Install and notifications
screens.content: Add to Home Screen (with iOS steps), 'Get new requests on this phone' after a tap, Sunlight theme offer.

items.request: Docs/40 SEC-WEB-5: the consumer BFF may also forward the provider operations of the Workshop PWA, as a named list of operation ids (not a path prefix): onboarding.list/update/accept_terms; org.location_create/update, org.location_pin_check; org.consents_list/grant; org.verification_submit; subscription.org_get; provider.profile_get/put, provider.publish, provider.service_category_create, provider.coverage_create, availability rule list/create; provider.appointments_list/get/transition, pre_visit.provider_get, provider.notes_list, provider.note_create, provider.calendar, provider.insights_get; reviews.org_list/get, review_responses.*, review_approvals.list/answer; provider.portfolio_list/get/create/update/consent_request/publish, media.redaction_decide; ai.review_response_draft, ai.showcase_compose, ai.appointment_suggestions; notifications with organization_id; the organization comment inbox of PRV-BR-02. The backend confirms with a test that these operations accept a cp-web-consumer token and that every other {org} operation is still refused at the consumer BFF.
items.why: PRV-GD-01. Today the consumer allowlist refuses all /v1/orgs/{org_id} routes except fleet driver routes.
items.fallback: None on the frontend except the allowlist code itself, which PW1 writes in pwa/. If the backend refuses cp-web-consumer for these operations, PW1 stops and the owner is asked.

items.request: cp-web-portal as a working BFF client: DPoP binding and private_key_jwt like cp-web-consumer (backend/libs/auth CLIENTS still says binding 'mtls', backend NI-08), a registered key in CARPAL_OAUTH_CLIENT_JWKS, redirect URIs for web.<DOMAIN> and local development, hosted sign-in under /id of the portal origin.
items.why: The portal BFF cannot sign in in strict mode without it.
items.fallback: PP1 builds and tests against lite mode (CARPAL_STRICT_AUTH=0); strict sign-in is checked in FT1a.

items.request: Web push sender (RFC 8030/8291/8292) with a VAPID key pair (pwa DI-72, OQ-26); the public key is set for pwa.<DOMAIN> and for web.<DOMAIN>.
items.fallback: Polling while the app is open, email, and SMS where enabled. Push controls stay hidden while no VAPID key is set, as today.

items.request: Push payload and tokens: (a) the payload carries organization_context_id and a target (type and id) besides notification_id and template_key (pwa DI-71); (b) web tokens of the consumer PWA and of the portal can be told apart (pwa DI-16), so a business push is not sent twice to one phone and a personal push is not sent to a portal-only install; (c) notification preferences can turn business pushes on and off per device.
items.why: With PRV-GD-01 the consumer PWA's worker receives business pushes and must open /provider/... for them.
items.fallback: A business push opens the notifications list of the business, where the row links to the page.

items.request: Notification event comment.created on the organization's content (to P+ members, respecting preferences); confirm that appointment.request_received, appointment.customer_message, review.received, review.approval_needed, review.approval_reminder and the showcase consent answers reach the provider members with the targets of this plan.
